name: custom-color-comment
description: Color comments based on custom tags like //! //? //TODO //////, fully configurable per-user via ccComment.tags in settings.json.

ccComment.tags.markdownDescription:
Map of comment tags to a color (hex string) or a style object. Merged on top of the built-in defaults (yours win on conflicts). Example:
```json
"ccComment.tags": {
  "!": "#FF0000",
  "?": "#121212",
  "TODO": { "color": "#00AEEF", "error": true, "errorColor": "blue", "errorWarning": true },
  "WARN": { "color": "#FFD700", "backgroundColor": "#332200", "backgroundOpacity": 0.4, "error": true, "errorColor": "yellow", "errorWarning": true },
  "BUG": { "color": "#FF3B3B", "error": true, "errorColor": "red", "errorWarning": true }
}
```
Set both `error: true` and `errorWarning: true` to create a native VS Code diagnostic for the entire matched comment. `errorColor` selects its severity and native squiggle color: `"blue"` = Information, `"yellow"` = Warning, `"red"` = Error. The squiggle is produced by the diagnostic API, not a text decoration. Add `ccComment:disable-errors` as a comment on the first line of a file to suppress these diagnostics in that file.

backgroundOpacity.description: Background opacity from 0 (transparent) to 1 (fully opaque). Requires backgroundColor.

lineThrough.description: Strike a line through the comment text.

error.description: Enable diagnostics for this tag when combined with errorWarning. Defaults to a yellow diagnostic if errorColor is not specified. String values remain supported for backward compatibility.

errorColor.description: Diagnostic severity and native squiggle color: blue = Information, yellow = Warning, red = Error. Defaults to yellow.

errorWarning.description: Create a native VS Code diagnostic and show the matched comment in the Problems panel. Requires error: true.

ccComment.disableDefaultTags.description: If true, only your custom ccComment.tags are used (built-in defaults are not merged in).
